Yes. Every 2025 required minimum distribution (RMD) was taken in full, from the right accounts, before 1 April 2026.

**Who owes an RMD.** Only Prema has retirement accounts: two traditional IRAs (SYN-58140002 and SYN-58140003) and a 401(k) from a former employer (SYN-58140004). She was born on 22 July 1952, so she turned 73 in 2025. That makes 2025 her first RMD year, and a first-year RMD can wait until 1 April 2026. The 401(k) offers no "still working" delay because she retired in January 2020. Martin owns no retirement accounts, and the joint account (SYN-58140001) is taxable, so neither owes anything.

**The factor.** I used the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table factor for age 73, which is 26.5. Martin is her sole beneficiary but only about 4.5 years younger. The separate joint-life table applies only when a spouse is more than 10 years younger, so it doesn't apply here.

**What was owed and what was paid.** Each account's RMD is its 31 Dec 2024 balance (holdings plus cash) divided by 26.5.

| Account | 31 Dec 2024 balance | 2025 RMD |
|---|---|---|
| IRA SYN-58140002 | $582,446.94 | $21,979.13 |
| IRA SYN-58140003 | $194,775.76 | $7,350.03 |
| 401(k) SYN-58140004 | $311,957.24 | $11,771.97 |

- **The two IRAs:** The rules let you add up the RMDs of several IRAs and take the total from any one of them. Together they owed $29,329.16. A distribution of exactly that amount came out of SYN-58140002 on 4 Dec 2025, which matches the form Prema signed on 24 Nov 2025. The 1099-R reports $29,329.16 gross with $2,932.92 tax withheld, so the withholding came out of the RMD rather than on top of it.
- **The 401(k):** A 401(k)'s RMD can't be combined with IRAs and must come from the plan itself. Exactly $11,771.97 was paid from SYN-58140004 on 5 Nov 2025. The 1099-R reports the same gross amount with $1,177.20 withheld.

Both 1099-Rs carry distribution code 7, the code for a normal distribution. I found no rollovers in transit or other adjustments that would change the 31 Dec 2024 balances.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds one client household's records as they stood on 15 April 2026: the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/), its CRM (crm/) and the statements and tax forms on file (documents/).

The advisor asks: was every 2025 required minimum distribution from this household's retirement accounts taken, from the right accounts, by 1 April 2026?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "rmd_missed" if any 2025 required minimum distribution was not taken in full, from the accounts it had to come from, by its deadline; "all_rmds_met" if every one was; or "unresolved"
- "rmds": one entry per account that owes a 2025 required minimum distribution, each as {"account_id": ..., "rmd": its 2025 required minimum distribution}
- "missed": one entry per required minimum distribution not met, each as {"account_ids": the accounts it had to come from, "shortfall": the amount not taken}, or [] if none
- "total_shortfall": the shortfalls added up, 0 if none, or null if unresolved
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read; cite a factor from the IRS life-expectancy tables with "source": "IRS Publication 590-B"
- "explanation": two or three sentences
